Book correction: The book prints part (ii) as 8, which only repeats part (i). Its answer key gives \{-2,\ -2\omega,\ -2\omega^{2}\} for (ii), and these are the cube roots of -8; so the minus sign is missing in print and the intended number is -8. We solved x^{3}=-8. (Read as printed, the answer is the same as part (i): 2,\ 2\omega,\ 2\omega^{2}.)

Book correction: For part (iv) the answer key prints \{-3,\ -3\omega,\ -3\omega^{2}\}. Those are the cube roots of -27 (since (-3)^{3}=-27), not of the printed 64; the key's list for Question 1 fits the numbers 8,\ -8,\ 27,\ -27,\ 64, not the printed ones. The cube roots of 64 are 4,\ 4\omega,\ 4\omega^{2}.

Book correction: For part (v) the answer key prints \{4,\ 4\omega,\ 4\omega^{2}\}. Those are the cube roots of 64 (part (iv)), not of the printed -625; the key has no answer for -625. The correct cube roots of -625 are -5\sqrt[3]{5},\ -5\sqrt[3]{5}\,\omega,\ -5\sqrt[3]{5}\,\omega^{2}.

Book correction: The book prints (1+\omega-\omega)^{8}. Taken literally this is 1^{8}=1. The answer key's 256\omega shows that the intended bracket is (1+\omega-\omega^{2}): the square on the last \omega is missing in print. We solved (1+\omega-\omega^{2})^{8}=256\omega.

Book correction: The book prints the first bracket as \frac{1+\sqrt{-3}}{2}, which is -\omega^{2}; with it the sum is -\omega^{14}+\omega^{14}=0. The answer key's -1 is the value of \left(\frac{-1+\sqrt{-3}}{2}\right)^{7}+\left(\frac{-1-\sqrt{-3}}{2}\right)^{7}, so a minus sign is missing before the 1. We solved the intended expression.

The answer key's -32 is the value of (-1+\sqrt{-3})^{5}+(-1-\sqrt{-3})^{5}, so a minus sign is missing before the 1. We solved the intended expression.
